examples.label: Local user accounts and their descriptions

notes:
=== User/Computer Description Field Credentials ===
Administrators misuse Description fields to store passwords — readable by all domain users.

=== WHY THIS HAPPENS ===
Active Directory Description field designed for administrative notes
Admins paste temporary passwords, notes, or reminders there for convenience
No understanding that ALL domain users can read this field by default
Common patterns: "Temp password: P@ssw0rd!", "Default pass: Welcome1", "Setup: Admin123"

=== COMMANDS ===
Local user description fields:
  Get-LocalUser | Select Name,Description,Enabled

Computer object description:
  Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_OperatingSystem | Select Description
  Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties Description | Select Name,Description

Domain user description fields:
  Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Description | Where-Object {$_.Description} | Select Name,Description

PowerView equivalent:
  Get-DomainUser -Properties description | Select samaccountname,description | Where-Object {$_.description}
  Get-DomainComputer -Properties description | Select name,description | Where-Object {$_.description}

=== OPERATIONAL NOTES ===
Entire field is readable without authentication to local system — only need domain user access
Takes less than 10 seconds to check — always run during initial enumeration
Findings are immediate: no cracking, no exploitation chain needed

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Description field → plaintext password → immediate credential use → lateral movement
Computer description → may contain service account credentials or admin notes
Service account description fields → sometimes contain passwords set by vendor documentation
After obtaining domain user credentials → immediately sweep all description fields via LDAP

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Any non-empty Description field on user or computer objects
Service accounts: description fields often set by vendors with default credential info
Computer objects: description may contain location, build info, and sometimes login credentials
Guest accounts and disabled accounts: may have plaintext passwords in description from initial setup
name: Credential Hunting - User & Computer Description Fields
description: Admins sometimes store passwords in the local-user or computer Description field. Quick to check and occasionally a free credential.

defense.why_it_works: AD user account description fields are readable by all authenticated domain users. Administrators sometimes store temporary passwords, account notes, or service account credentials in description fields for convenience. These are exposed via Get-LocalUser, Get-ADUser, or net user.
defense.prerequisites: Any authenticated domain or local account. LDAP query or net user access to enumerate account descriptions.
defense.impact: Plaintext credential discovery from AD description fields, enabling account takeover or privilege escalation if an admin password or service account password is stored there.
defense.detection: Mass LDAP query of user objects' description attribute. Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Description executed by standard user. SIEM: large LDAP query patterns suggesting AD enumeration.
defense.artifacts: LDAP query log: attribute read on description field | Process log: Get-LocalUser / Get-ADUser executed by non-admin
defense.prevention: Audit all AD user description fields for credential data. Never store passwords in description fields — use a secrets manager. Implement AD attribute auditing. Regular Active Directory hygiene checks.
defense.misconfiguration: Help desk or admin sets a temporary password in a user account's description field and forgets to clear it. Service accounts have their passwords documented in description for convenience.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# AD user description contains password:
Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Description | select Name,Description
# Output: svc_backup | AdminPass2024!

# Local users:
Get-LocalUser | select Name,Description
defense.secure_config:
# Audit description fields
Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Description | Where-Object {$_.Description -match 'pass|pwd|cred'}

# Clear credential data from description fields
Set-ADUser -Identity svc_backup -Description ''

# Use LAPS or PAM for privileged account credentials
# Implement AD attribute auditing policy
